## How this deck works {.smaller}

This is a **living timeline** of progress on Chapter 2.

- The nightly pipeline appends a date-stamped section after midnight every day.
- Each daily section includes a short summary of what was worked on plus any new figures.
- Newest entries appear at the **bottom** — navigate forward (→) through time, backward (←) for older.

For the curated talk version, see [chapter2-slides.html](chapter2-slides.html).

## Status legend

- ✅ figure finalized for chapter
- 🔄 figure under iteration
- ⚠ result preliminary, do not cite

. . .

The "What we did" lines are pulled from the daily-summaries the nightly loop writes; figures are mirrored from `chapter-2-volc-enso/figures/`.

# 2026-08-30 {.center}

::: {.under-review}

## What we did

- Automation-only window (08-29 → 08-30): no substantive user sessions touched Ch2.
- The 23 figures synced on 08-25 remain held out of chapter prose, still awaiting the `ch3_` vs `ch3r_` variant choice and confirmation that the `ch3` prefix is the source project's numbering rather than dissertation Chapter 3.

## New literature

- He et al. 2026 — SEA across tree-ring reconstructions, nine data-assimilation products and two model ensembles; global cooling robust, but persistence diverges by proxy type (ring density short and physically consistent, ring width longer via biological memory), and the **ENSO response differs across products**, implying a volcanic ENSO signal weak against internal variability [@he2026volcaniccomparison]
- Tripp et al. 2026 — Galápagos corals at ~4 ka show ENSO variance comparable to 1959–1979 CE but *negatively* skewed, a reminder that the El Niño-like framing tested here is a property of the recent baseline rather than of ENSO in general [@tripp2026galapagos]
- Implication for this chapter's SEA composites: agreement between two reconstructions is not by itself evidence of a forced response, and the methods text should state how much of the apparent post-eruption anomaly could come from archive properties and sampling

:::

# 2026-08-25 {.center}

::: {.under-review}

## What we did

- Covered the 2026-08-19 → 2026-08-25 window after three consecutive aborted pipeline runs (08-19, 08-20, 08-22).
- `sync_figures.sh` copied **23 new figures** from the `volcano enso` source project into this chapter's `figures/` folder — the first genuinely new figure arrivals since 2026-08-09. Source mtimes span 08-20 through 08-25.
- Figures were **deliberately not auto-inserted into `chapter2.qmd`** this run. Two reasons, both needing C's judgement rather than an automated guess.

## Why these figures are held for review

- **Six arrived as duplicate pairs.** `fig01_eruption_catalog`, `fig03_sea_per_eruption`, `fig06_spatial_composite`, `fig07_iso2k_multi`, `fig09_forcing_response_scatter` and `fig10_summary_matrix` each exist in both a `ch3_` and a `ch3r_` variant, and `fig04` exists as both `sea_composite` and `sea_composite_dualbaseline`. Inserting every file would place two versions of the same figure in the chapter; choosing between them is a curation call.
- **The filename prefix contradicts the destination.** All 23 are named `ch3_*` or `ch3r_*` but the sync routed them into Chapter 2. The subject matter — eruption catalog, superposed-epoch composites, iso2k and pseudo-coral comparisons, Niño 3.4 correlations — is squarely Chapter 2's, so the prefix most likely reflects the source project's own internal numbering rather than dissertation Chapter 3. That is an inference, not a confirmation, and it is worth C settling before the figures are cited.

## New literature

- None for this chapter. The single reference added this run (Gruber & Sarmiento 1997, defining the N* nitrate–phosphate tracer) went to Chapter 4's bibliography only, for the N* maps added there.

:::
